# Sweep 25 — THE THIRTEEN-ROUND RACE (2026-08-11)

**Generated by a measurement, not the wheel.** Our median kill round is **174**,
our median death round is **187**, and our core dies in **46.3% of all games**.
We are not losing to a strategy on a different timescale — we are losing a photo
finish, roughly half the time, to opponents doing approximately the same thing to
us at approximately the same moment. Four arms: (A) who diagnosed a close race
and what did they *change*; (B) ⭐ tempo vs robustness at the margin; (C) the
variance argument; (D) interception and the cost of being stopped once.

Run at `2026-08-11T19:05:22Z` (`date -u`), against commit `7fc3971`.

---

and one CodinGame Ocean of Code writeup.

| **repairs made BY the end-to-end audit** | **25.** 21 spans failed only on **straight vs curly apostrophes** in my draft and were normalised to the sources' `’` so they verify byte-exact. **4 were real defects: 3 of my OWN GLOSSES were sitting inside quotation marks** (smite's halt-vs-reserve contrast, and two measurement-event definitions) and were de-quoted; **1 was a paraphrase of `CLAUDE.md`** — I had written *"numbers carry subjects — copy the denominator…"* where the source reads **"Numbers carry subjects."** … **"Copy the denominator, the population, and the clock along with the number."** Now quoted as two spans with the splice declared. **This is sweep 24's failure mode (paraphrase-into-unmarked-text) reproducing in a new sweep, caught only by the mechanical check.** |

Caught by reading the `<title>` and `href` out of the saved `.raw`. **The quote was verbatim; the citation was invented** — a new instance of the index's second rule (verbatim is necessary and not sufficient) landing in the *source* field rather than the text. |
| **page furniture shown, not spliced** | 1 — confused 2020's failed-rush sentence contains the injected running header `Battlecode 2020 Postmortem 15`; reproduced with the furniture and flagged in-file. |

**⚠ ONE REAL HOLE IN THE CENSUS, and it sits where a counterexample would live.**
**Liquipedia's `Timing Attack`, `All-in` and `Tempo` articles were NOT read.**
The fetch returned Cloudflare rate-limit pages whose own text instructs automated
agents to halt rather than work around the block; the download agent complied and
left nothing on disk. Those are the field's canonical documents on *timing
attacks* — the single topic most likely to falsify arm B's negative. **Anyone
re-running arm B should obtain them by hand first.**

## ⭐ ARM B, STATED PLAINLY — a negative and a positive, and the positive dissolves the question

**THE NEGATIVE IS HARD AND IT IS QUANTIFIED.** Nobody in this field has measured
the tempo/robustness trade, because nobody has ever made arrival time a dependent
variable. Over 222,488 words: `kill round` **0** · `time to win` **0** ·
`game length` **0** · `won faster` **0** · `tempo cost` **0** · `traded tempo`
**0** · `delayed our attack` **0** · `delaying the attack` **0** — 29 of 32
duration/trade phrasings return exactly zero. The one `game duration` hit is a
*simulation horizon* inside a CodinGame search, not an outcome, and is reported
in-file so the lone non-zero cannot be reconstructed into a counterexample. This
extends sweep 24's negative onto a corpus 58% larger and sharpens it: the field
A/Bs constantly (`scrim` 120, `tested` 28, `AB test` 7) and **the outcome
variable is always the win rate.**
→ [`nobody-separated-tempo-from-robustness`](nobody-separated-tempo-from-robustness.md)

**THE POSITIVE IS THAT THE DICHOTOMY IS FALSE, and one author worked it out.**
Only four spans in the entire corpus treat *delay* as a quantity to be protected
(`critical path` 1, `no delay` 1, `without delaying` 2) — **all four are Jay
Scott, in one three-post series, about one build order.** His answer to "faster
or harder to stop" is **neither: fund the robustness out of INCOME rather than
off the CRITICAL PATH, and you get both.** He writes two builds that buy the same
escort, and rejects the one that pays for it by deleting a worker:

> *"I do not recommend the A version above. I think the B version below is
> better. It keeps the 9th drone and gets the 2 zergling pairs later. With the
> income from the 9th drone, it is possible to get the same 4 zerglings without
> delaying the lurkers."*

**This is `DEFENCE_ADMISSION_BAR: kill_round_non_regression` expressed as a
construction rule instead of a post-hoc bar** — the purchase is made to pass the
bar at design time. It is the same idea as sweep 24's most buildable item
([`the-rush-cost-budget-gate`](the-rush-cost-budget-gate.md)) approached from the
other side: the rush cost makes non-rush spending *expensive*; the critical-path
rule makes it *free exactly where it is free* and forbidden elsewhere.
→ [`buy-the-escort-out-of-income-not-off-the-critical-path`](buy-the-escort-out-of-income-not-off-the-critical-path.md)

**AND THE CHAMPION DID NOT SEPARATE THEM.** Just Woke Up's BC2025 finals patch
contains a tempo change (b-line to a remembered build site, **gated on the unit's
own affordability**) and a robustness change (**temporal** staggering into enemy
tower range) *two sentences apart*, reported under one pooled figure —
*"minor optimization here and there that great boosted our winrate against our
old bot versions"* — by a team that owned an automated all-map A/B harness and
used it elsewhere in the same document. **The strongest team in the corpus had
the instrument, had both halves of arm B in one patch, and pooled anyway.**
→ [`the-champions-margin-patch-bought-both-and-measured-neither`](the-champions-margin-patch-bought-both-and-measured-neither.md)

## THE OTHER ARMS

**ARM A — two teams diagnosed a race and shipped a named mechanism.**
**smite (BC2019)** identified a race to contested clusters, flagged the operative
phrase themselves (*"there’s one keyword here: as early as possible"*), and
shipped a **team-wide one-turn spending freeze** so the shared bank could afford
the racing unit — *"If I’m not the closest castle … I return immediately, halting
all production for one turn"* — and reported the result **as an arrival round**,
which almost nothing else in the corpus does: *"our harassers emerge from castles
around turn 4-6, early enough to beat enemies to most clusters."* We have six
titanium **floors** and no **halt**; `eco.py` never defers to the raid.
→ [`halt-the-other-spenders-so-the-racing-unit-lands-early`](halt-the-other-spenders-so-the-racing-unit-lands-early.md)

**ARM C — the distribution question is nearly empty, and the one team that acted
on it lost.** Exactly one span in 222,488 words reasons about the spread of one's
own arrival time (Jay Scott: *"maybe the timings should give low and high values,
or mean and variance, or something"*) and it is an **explicitly unbuilt
proposal** resting on cross-game persistence our sandbox forbids.
→ [`the-only-mean-versus-variance-proposal-was-never-built`](the-only-mean-versus-variance-proposal-was-never-built.md)
The one team that shipped a mean-for-variance trade — **Oak's Last Disciple**,
who wrote *"consistency is really valuable"*, computed which of their bots was
*"the most consistent one"* and submitted it — **lost, and diagnosed why
themselves**: *"Our assumption that the eco bot was the most consistent was
assuming that there would be a relatively equal proportion of the strategies
described."* The population moved. **That is sweep 22's non-stationarity finding
with a tournament exit attached.**
→ [`the-consistency-choice-that-lost-the-tournament`](the-consistency-choice-that-lost-the-tournament.md)
The structurally useful arm-C result is Jay Scott's crosstable argument: **a
strong bot's losses are concentrated against opponents it usually beats**, because
that is where nearly all its loss opportunities are. Combined with the
`target_value` gate — a win down there pays almost nothing — this says **upside
is negligible and the entire downside distribution lives in the matchups we
already win.** Our 46.3% core-death rate on a 13-round margin is that signature.
→ [`your-losses-land-against-opponents-you-usually-beat`](your-losses-land-against-opponents-you-usually-beat.md)

**ARM D — no team anywhere prices a failed push in rounds. Two supply the
shape.** **confused (BC2020)** price it from the attacker's side and the answer
is that a stopped push still paid: *"even if the rush failed, it was still very
damaging to recover from the rush if it's even halfway successful"* — the residue
was **terrain that outlived every attacking unit**. ⚠ **We already ship this**
(`raid.py:55`, *"barriers deposited on the first action after landing (value that
outlives the body)"*), so this file confirms a shipped plank from an independent
source rather than proposing one — and it carries a correction: our residue must
be **additive** (our barrier on their tile), never **subtractive**, because
destroying their buildings LOWERS their scale.
→ [`the-failed-push-still-leaves-a-crater`](the-failed-push-still-leaves-a-crater.md)
**om nom (BC2025)** answer the resumability half with a liveness invariant:
*"Whenever our estimated number of Paint Towers hit 0, we would just build
another one."*
→ [`rebuild-on-zero-needs-a-counter-that-can-reach-zero`](rebuild-on-zero-needs-a-counter-that-can-reach-zero.md)

**AND ONE FILE FROM THE SIDE WE ARE ACTUALLY ON.** Jay Scott records a bot that
**won the opening race and then bought safety with the lead**: *"instead of
making a second hatchery to win with mass lings, or getting quick gas to win with
mutalisks, KillAll turtled. It threw away its advantage."* Both rejected
alternatives are conversions of the lead into a *faster follow-up*. Reconciled
with s30's measured negatives (`home-turrets-off` 433/1024, `barrier-seal-off`
399/1024 — removing defence COST us): the rule bites on defence bought **with a
lead**, a narrower case than defence bought at all.
→ [`converting-a-won-race-into-safety-threw-the-game`](converting-a-won-race-into-safety-threw-the-game.md)

**AND THE ONLY RULE IN THE CORPUS ABOUT WHEN A DEFENSIVE PURCHASE SHOULD BEGIN**
(sweep 24 covered when it should *end*): Jay Scott's *"Don’t build sunks too
early"*, keyed to the opponent's recorded first-attack timing, with the downside
accepted out loud — *"If a clever enemy notices the vulnerability and attacks
early, too bad."* Our engine makes deferral unusually cheap: scale is additive
and time-independent, so deferring a **+20%** purchase avoids inflating every
intervening build for those rounds, and ammo converts 1:1 **the same turn**, so
late defence is not handicapped by an empty bank.
→ [`time-the-defensive-purchase-to-their-measured-attack`](time-the-defensive-purchase-to-their-measured-attack.md)

## THE SINGLE MOST BUILDABLE ITEM

**[`rebuild-on-zero-needs-a-counter-that-can-reach-zero`](rebuild-on-zero-needs-a-counter-that-can-reach-zero.md)
— and it is buildable because the bug is already documented in our own tree,
twice, by name.**

om nom's plank needs a count that can fall. Our tree has hit that exact failure
three times:

| slot | status | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `SLOT_FWD_GUN` | **FIXED** (LOKI-2b, live census `_live_fwd_guns`) | `doctrine.py:1222` — *"counts every forward sentinel we have EVER built, alive or dead. Three destroyed turrets close the forward-sentinel arm PERMANENTLY"* |
| `SLOT_LAUNCHER` | **FIXED** (LOKI-6) | `doctrine.py:1427` — *"cleared ONLY on a failed build -- never on death … Same shape as the SLOT_FWD_GUN rubble counter that LOKI-2b had to fix."* |
| **`SLOT_HARVESTERS`** | **NOT FIXED** | `doctrine.py:381` — *"a monotone high-water mark of harvesters BUILT"*; `eco.py:381-382` is a one-way ratchet |

`eco.py:381` **already computes `live`** and discards it whenever it is smaller.
The counter can rise and can never fall, so it can never reach zero, so the
rebuild trigger cannot fire — while `raid.py:409` gates the entire siege on it.
**Same defect class, third instance, and this one holds an arm open on an economy
that may be dead.**

**HOOK — no new store slot** (the 16 are fully bound, `doctrine.py:931-961`,
remapped `:1166-1170`, so a slot-hungry plank is not buildable as written; **this
one is not**). Use the **local** `live` value already on that line as a rebuild
trigger, and keep publishing only the monotone high-water mark to the slot so no
existing reader changes behaviour: *if `live == 0` and `read_store(SLOT_HARVESTERS) >= 1`,
promote harvester rebuild to the top of this builder's action priority.* Guard it
the way `_live_fwd_guns` is guarded — return early unless the unit is close
enough for a zero to mean **absence** rather than **blindness**. That guard is the
whole plank; without it this is an alarm that cannot tell it is blind.

**PREDICTED EFFECT ON MEDIAN KILL ROUND: NEUTRAL-TO-EARLIER, and testable in both
directions.** It buys no HP and no screening — it replaces a stale belief with a
true one. It should kill **earlier** in games where we were siege-gating off a
phantom economy; it can kill **later** only where the phantom count was
accidentally carrying us past a gate we would otherwise have failed. Both are
real, which is why it needs the bar rather than an argument.

## WHAT THIS SWEEP DID NOT FIND, recorded so it is not re-chased

* **No figure anywhere for "one failed push = N rounds."** Arm D's headline
  question has no answer in the field; nobody counts it.
* **No shipped mean-for-variance trade on ARRIVAL TIME.** One unbuilt proposal.
* **No constant, threshold or exchange rate for the tempo/robustness trade.**
* **`transfers: no` count: 1** (the arm-B census). `yes`: 4. `partial`: 6.
* **The Liquipedia hole above.** It is the one place a counterexample to arm B's
  negative would most plausibly live.
